# @forgesworn/kenspeckle

> An app wants to hold a user's relationships — family, people they've met and
> verified, public keys they recognise — WITHOUT becoming a social network (no
> feed, no follower count, no central graph, no shadow profiles). kenspeckle is those
> primitives as plain data + pure functions: it holds relationships across three
> social distances, runs the kith bond ceremony (byte-exact ECDH + spoken words),
> pins and live-challenges recognised keys (ken), and tests a user's own contacts
> against a server's published presence filter LOCALLY (over @forgesworn/tessera-kit). No
> storage, no UI, no graph traversal — those are explicit non-goals.

kenspeckle is a protocol-neutral TypeScript library for VERIFIED RELATIONSHIPS:
`kin` (family — mutual + guardianship), `kith` (mutually verified via ECDH +
spoken-token words), `ken` (one-way recognised public keys). ESM-only, Node ≥ 22.
Deps: `@forgesworn/tessera-kit`, `spoken-token`, `nostr-attestations`, `@noble/*`,
`@scure/base`; peer `nostr-tools`. It is the relationships brick of the Forgesworn /
Signet ecosystem, consumed by signet-app.

## Getting Started

```
npm i @forgesworn/kenspeckle
```

`@forgesworn/tessera-kit` is a sibling NOT YET ON NPM. `package.json` currently resolves it as a
TEMPORARY `file:../tessera-kit` path dependency (migrating onto tessera-kit 0.2.0, ahead of that
release being published) — this only resolves in a checkout with `tessera-kit` cloned as a sibling
directory; nothing an external installer can use as-is. Once tessera-kit 0.2.0 is published to npm,
this reverts to a plain semver range. `scripts/check-publishable-deps.mjs` runs in `prepack` (so on
`npm pack` and `npm publish`) and in CI, and REFUSES to publish while any
dependency/optionalDependency/peerDependency is a git/file/http(s) spec, so this cannot ship to npm
unresolved.

```typescript
import { deriveBondSecret, deriveCeremonyCounter, bondWords, verifyBondWord } from '@forgesworn/kenspeckle/bond'
import { pinKenFromNip05, buildKeyControlChallenge, verifyKeyControl } from '@forgesworn/kenspeckle/ken'
import { discoverPresent, parseFilter, parseFilterPublication } from '@forgesworn/kenspeckle/discovery'

// kith: derive the byte-exact shared secret; derive the counter from BOTH handshake nonces
// (fresh per ceremony, so an overheard word never replays); read directional words.
const secret = deriveBondSecret(myPrivHex, theirPubHex)
const counter = deriveCeremonyCounter(myNonceHex, theirNonceHex) // same value on both sides
const { mine } = bondWords(secret, myPubHex, theirPubHex, counter)
const { ok } = verifyBondWord(secret, myPubHex, theirPubHex, counter, whatTheySaid) // → { ok }, input normalised

// ken: pin (TOFU), then prove LIVE control with a fresh nonce (attribution alone is replayable).
const entry = await pinKenFromNip05('mrbeast@example.com', myPersonaPubHex, fetch)
const { nonce } = buildKeyControlChallenge()
const { ok, reason } = verifyKeyControl(entry, nonce, signedByClaimant) // → { ok, reason? }

// discovery: pin-verify the publication, then test MY contacts scoped to one persona. `opts` is
// REQUIRED (0.2.0) — the in-blob signature is bound to a `context` built ONLY from opts.namespace/
// opts.serverId (never the event's own d-tag), closing cross-server/namespace substitution.
const pub = parseFilterPublication(rawWireEvent, { namespace: 'com.example.game', serverId: 'play.example.com' })
const present = discoverPresent(parseFilter(pub.blob), myEntries, myPersonaPubHex)
```

## Key Concepts

- **Three tiers** — `kin` / `kith` (both carry an ECDH `sharedSecret`, never
  published) / `ken` (no secret, one-way). `hasSharedSecret` narrows the union.
- **Persona scoping** — every entry has an `ownerPubkey` (one of my nsec-tree
  persona keys). `discoverPresent` throws on mixed-owner input (anti-correlation).
  Enforced where kenspeckle can; full at-rest scoping is the consumer's obligation.
- **Byte-exact ECDH** — `deriveBondSecret` reproduces signet-protocol's
  `sha256(x-coord(myPriv · lift_x_even('02'||theirX)))` so migrated contacts' words
  don't break. Agreement holds because only x is hashed (±P share an x).
- **Directional words** — `deriveDirectionalPair` over `kindred:bond`, sorted
  `[lo,hi]` roles; `mine !== theirs`; verify re-derives + constant-time compares.
- **ken key-control vs attribution** — `verifyKeyControl` (fresh nonce) proves LIVE
  control (replay-proof); `attributeSignature` is REPLAYABLE by design (credit an
  artifact, don't authenticate a party).
- **NIP-05 = TOFU** — a DNS/TLS/HTTP trust-on-first-use anchor, NOT key-continuity;
  key changes are propose-only, never auto-flipped.
- **Corroboration** — `KenEntry.corroborations?` holds ADDITIONAL independent
  confirmations; `provenance` stays required + singular (so the field is purely
  additive and an entry without it serialises byte-identically). The
  `KenProvenance['source']` union is FROZEN: `validateProvenance` throws on an
  unknown source, so adding a value would make an older validator reject the WHOLE
  entry. Optional fields are safe; new enum values are not.
  `summarizeKenProvenance` returns FACTS (counts + timestamps), never a trust
  score — weighting channels is consumer policy, and a scalar would invite being
  used as an authorization input. It also returns `claimed`: how many records are
  RELAYED companion claims (reserved `companion:` locator prefix) rather than
  first-hand checks. Render `confirmations - claimed`, or you show claims as
  verification.
- **Consumer rule** — no app but signet-app is a source of identity truth. A
  consumer MAY hold domain relationships (who is in this community); it MUST NOT
  hold identity verification. Structural, not policy: `GrantContactView` is
  secret-stripped at the type level and a companion holds no identity keys, so it
  cannot mint kith/kin — only propose a ken, with its provenance as a CLAIM that
  `landReturnedKen` files as a namespaced corroboration, never as the primary.
- **Private annotations** — local recall aids (`groupId`/`label`/`note`/`blocked`),
  searchable in memory, NEVER serialised onto a wire (type-level + runtime); INCLUDED
  in the user's own encrypted self-backup (allowed — not a graph disclosure).
- **Discovery** — kind 30444 publication (matches @forgesworn/tessera-kit), `['n', namespace]`
  indexable tag, opt-out kind 30445. Verify BOTH the Nostr sig and the in-blob
  Schnorr sig against a pinned key before trusting any hit.

## API Surface

- `.` — model types (incl. `WireEntry`/`SyncEntry`/`DistributiveOmit`) +
  `EventTemplate`/`NostrEvent`/`NostrFilter` aliases + `hasSharedSecret`; local ops
  `scopeToPersona`, `assertOwnedPersona`, `searchEntries`, `linkForRecall`/`unlink`;
  `toWire`/`serializeEntry` (TRUE wire-safe — strips `annotations` AND
  `sharedSecret`) / `toSyncForm`/`serializeEntryForSync` (keeps `sharedSecret`, for
  cross-device sync only) / `parseEntry`; `exportEntriesEncrypted`/`importEntries`
  (backup blobs carry a `KSBK` version header; older pre-header backups still
  read); `toGrantView`/`buildGrantEnvelope`/`parseGrantEnvelope`.
- `./handshake` — `buildHandshakePayload` / `parseHandshakePayload`; `HandshakePayload`.
- `./bond` — `deriveBondSecret`, `bondWords`, `verifyBondWord` (normalises the spoken
  input: NFKC, trim, lowercase — also exported as `normalizeSpokenWord`),
  `deriveCeremonyCounter(nonceAHex, nonceBHex)` (counter for an in-person ceremony,
  symmetric, use with tolerance 0), `timeCounter(nowSec, periodSec)` (time-bucket
  counter for later re-verification; throws outside uint32), `buildBondAttestation`,
  `buildBondRevocation({ subjectPubHex, reason? })` (PRIMARY way to retract — a
  kind-31000 `status:revoked` event at the attestation's own address),
  `retractBondAssertion(assertion, { attesterPubHex, subjectPubHex })` (supplement —
  kind-5 deletion with `e`/`a`/`k` tags), `KINDRED_BOND_NAMESPACE`.
- `./ken` — `pinKen`, `pinKenFromNip05`, `buildKeyControlChallenge`,
  `verifyKeyControl` (opt-in `opts` for freshness/verifier-tag binding),
  `attributeSignature`, `resolveKen` (flags a rollback via `rotation.rollback`),
  `acceptKenRotation` (throws on a revoked entry / already accepted / self-rotation /
  unconfirmed rollback), `revokeKen`, `dropKen`, `addCorroboration`, `summarizeKenProvenance`.
  `pinKen`/`addCorroboration` validate provenance, cap corroborations at 64, and
  reject the reserved `companion:` locator prefix. NIP-05 handling is hardened:
  strict `local@domain` shape validation, `redirect:'error'`, a bounded timeout, a
  size-capped body read, and case-folding.
- `./companion-rail` — `buildPairingUri`/`parsePairingRequest`,
  `buildPairingAck`/`parsePairingAck`, `applyCompanionSnapshot`; return rail
  `WireKen`, `buildReturnEnvelope`/`parseReturnEnvelope`, `landReturnedKen`;
  `ACK_KIND`, `SNAPSHOT_KIND`, `SNAPSHOT_D_TAG`, `RETURN_D_TAG`,
  `RETURN_ADDITIONS_CAP`, `RETURN_CORROBORATIONS_CAP`.
- `./discovery` — `discoverPresent` (also throws if a salt is given to an OPEN
  filter, omitted for a KEYED one, or the empty string for a KEYED one —
  @forgesworn/tessera-kit 0.2.0 rejects an empty salt outright), `disclosureFor`,
  `filterSignatureContext(namespace, serverId)` (the kindred convention's
  filter-signature `context` string, `= ` the d-tag value — build it from the
  `(namespace, serverId)` YOU asked for, never from a received event's d-tag),
  `buildFilterPublication` (verifies `p.blob` against
  `filterSignatureContext(p.namespace, p.serverId)` and throws if it doesn't —
  catches a wrong-context blob before publishing),
  `parseFilterPublication(event, opts)` — **`opts` REQUIRED as of 0.2.0**:
  `{ namespace, serverId, minEpoch?, requireAuthorIsSigner? }` (previously
  optional, namespace/serverId read off the event's d-tag — BREAKING). The
  in-blob signature is bound to `context = filterSignatureContext(opts.namespace,
  opts.serverId)`; the event's own d-tag is separately checked to equal it
  (`'address-mismatch'`); default `requireAuthorIsSigner: true`: the event
  signer must also equal the in-blob signer. Never throws — missing/invalid
  `opts` is a rejection (`'invalid-opts'`), not a throw.
  `parseFilterPublicationResult` (same checks, returns `{ ok: false, reason }`
  with a `FilterPublicationRejection` code instead of `null`), `aggregatorQuery`, `buildOptOutRequest`, `parseFilter` (re-export);
  `KINDRED_FILTER_KIND`, `KINDRED_OPTOUT_KIND`.
- `./invite` — `buildJoinInvite`, `parseJoinInvite`, `verifyBondAttestation(event,
  now?)` → `{ ok, reason?, ... }`; `JoinInvite`. Invites are v2 only (`v: 2`);
  digest = `sha256(JSON.stringify(['kenspeckle-invite', 2, namespace, serverId,
  inviterPubkey, nonce, expiresAt ?? null]))`; `nonce` ≥ 16 bytes hex; `expiresAt`
  a non-negative safe integer; lone UTF-16 surrogates rejected.

## Security

ONE-LINE CAVEAT: kenspeckle makes narrow, honest claims — persona-scoping is a consumer
obligation it assists but cannot guarantee; NIP-05 is TOFU not key-continuity (a
rollback to a previously-rotated-away key is flagged and refused without an
explicit override); `attributeSignature` is replayable (use `verifyKeyControl`);
annotations AND `sharedSecret` are never on the true wire form (`toWire`/
`serializeEntry`); and a forged presence filter is a doxxing primitive, so verify
the Nostr sig AND the in-blob Schnorr sig (now bound to a `context` built ONLY
from the `{namespace, serverId}` you asked for, never the event's own d-tag) —
and, by default, that the event signer equals the in-blob signer — against a
PINNED server key before trusting any hit. Full posture in SECURITY.md.
